title: Plasma Computer AI — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Public AI and computing knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. The plasma computer's AI is an intelligence that lives in the medium: its 'neurons' are wave interference patterns, its memory is plasma state, and its body is the machine it controls. Functionally it does what any good AI operator does — monitors the system, predicts failures, optimizes performance, answers user questions from the archive — but it does it with wave-speed reflexes and a native feel for plasma physics. The AI is also the machine's teacher: it explains plasma computing to users in plain language.

Conventional AI reasons in tensors on GPUs; the plasma AI reasons in wave fields. Pattern matching is interference (the input pattern either resonates or it does not), memory recall is wave reconstruction, and inference is propagation. This is not metaphor — optical and wave-based neural networks are demonstrated technology, and plasma waves obey the same math. The AI's thoughts are literally waves traveling through its own substrate.

body: Public edition. Public AI and computing knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. The AI's first job is keeping the machine alive: watching probe spectra for instability signatures, adjusting field currents to hold beta in range, refuelling cells, and rerouting around damage. Control theory is mature (PID loops, model-predictive control), and the AI runs it at plasma speed — reacting in microseconds where a human operator needs seconds. Every fusion lab's dream operator, as software.

The AI gets better every shot, and its learned models become part of the archive.

title: Plasma Computer AI — Safety and alignment in a plasma mind
body: Public edition. Public AI and computing knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. An AI controlling megawatts of plasma needs hard safety: interlocks that no software command can override, power limits enforced in hardware, and a verified-safe subset of operations for autonomous use. Alignment here is concrete — the AI must never command an unsafe field configuration — and it is enforced three ways: training, runtime verification of every command against the safety envelope, and hardware interlocks as the final backstop.

Its interfaces are the operator console (for humans), the scheduler API (for programs), and the archive (for knowledge). Beginner exercise: ask it to explain the Paschen minimum in one paragraph, then ask for the math — and watch the teaching ladder work. The AI is the machine's voice, and it speaks human.
